Close the Books on February

MediumFree

February is closed. Finance keeps closed months out of the live orders table and in orders_archive, an empty table with the same columns as orders.

Move every completed February order from orders into orders_archive, every column as it is, so that it is in the archive and no longer in orders. February orders that are pending or cancelled stay in orders for the team to chase. Nothing from January or March moves.

The move must never stop halfway: either both tables change or neither does.

Graded on both tables after your statements run, on a fresh copy each attempt.

Solve it in the browser editor →

Runs on SQLite in your browser, on a fresh copy of the tables every attempt, and is graded on what the table holds after your statements. No signup. A wrong answer says how your table differs, not just "incorrect". Free accounts get 10 free challenge solves, and this can be one of them.

Expected output: orders_archive: February's completed orders; orders: January, March, and February's pending and cancelled

Hint

Two changes that must go together: copy the rows into the archive, then remove the same rows from orders. Use exactly the same condition for both. February has 29 days in 2024.
